title: Mandala Checkered Fill Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: This mandala design sits on the palm. The main fill is lotus pattern, with floral vine worked around it. It's on the harder side, and it suits Teej.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
In Indian and Pakistani mehndi, this round design is commonly called a tikki or gol tikki. The design depends on symmetry: each ring repeats the same shape all the way around.
Application tips: Wash and dry the skin before application and skip lotion or oil, which block the dye. Keeping the skin warm while the paste is on helps the colour develop.

image.alt: Mandala Checkered Fill mehndi design for front hand henna pattern

faq.q: Should I do a patch test before applying mehndi?
faq.a: Yes. Apply a small amount of the paste to the inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if you have sensitive skin or are using a new cone.

faq.q: What does mandala mean in mehndi?
faq.a: It refers to a circular design built from repeating rings around a centre point.

faq.q: Is a mandala the same as a tikki design?
faq.a: A tikki is a round mandala placed on the palm or back of the hand, usually with decorated fingertips.

title: Mandala Butterfly Wing Mehndi Design for Arm
descriptionParagraphs: Mandala style, arm placement. You'll see lotus pattern and butterfly wing in it. We'd call it expert to draw, and a nice pick for Karva Chauth.

Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

Mandala means circle in Sanskrit, and mandala mehndi is built from rings of petals and patterns around a central point. A mandala in the centre of the palm or the back of the hand is one of the most recognisable mehndi layouts.
Application tips: Start with a small circle in the centre and add one ring at a time. Turn the hand, not the cone, as you work around the circle to keep the petals even.

image.alt: Mandala Butterfly Wing mehndi design for arm henna pattern

faq.q: What does mandala mean in mehndi?
faq.a: It refers to a circular design built from repeating rings around a centre point.

faq.q: Is a mandala the same as a tikki design?
faq.a: A tikki is a round mandala placed on the palm or back of the hand, usually with decorated fingertips.

faq.q: Are mandala designs suitable for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. A basic mandala uses only circles, petals and dots, and it can be made more detailed as you improve.

title: Mandala Teardrop Cascade Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: Look at the teardrop cascade first, then the sunburst that frames it. This one is made for the fingers and is easy enough for a first try. Wear it for Diwali.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This is a beginner-friendly pattern: practise the main shapes on paper first, then copy them onto skin with a fine-tipped cone.
In Indian and Pakistani mehndi, this round design is commonly called a tikki or gol tikki. The design depends on symmetry: each ring repeats the same shape all the way around.
Application tips: Finish with a ring of dots; it hides small unevenness in the outer edge. Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain.

image.alt: Mandala Teardrop Cascade mehndi design for finger henna pattern

faq.q: Is a mandala the same as a tikki design?
faq.a: A tikki is a round mandala placed on the palm or back of the hand, usually with decorated fingertips.

faq.q: Are mandala designs suitable for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. A basic mandala uses only circles, petals and dots, and it can be made more detailed as you improve.

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?
faq.a: A natural henna stain usually lasts one to three weeks. It fades faster on areas that are washed or rubbed often, such as the hands.

title: Mandala Dotwork Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A mandala pattern for the back of the hand, built from checkered fill and heart vine. Difficulty: expert. Good for Eid.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

Mandala means circle in Sanskrit, and mandala mehndi is built from rings of petals and patterns around a central point. A mandala in the centre of the palm or the back of the hand is one of the most recognisable mehndi layouts.

Application tips: Dab a lemon and sugar mixture on the dried paste to keep it moist and stuck to the skin. Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours.

image.alt: Mandala Dotwork mehndi design for back hand henna pattern

faq.q: How long does a mehndi stain last?

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.
